# Linked scrolling fixture

Scroll either pane: the other follows through the scroll anchors. Long paragraphs below are **one source line each**, so they wrap to many rows in the editor and render as one block in the preview.

## 1. Lighthouse keeping

Everything about lighthouse keeping starts at the lamp room, where the work is quiet and slow and nobody hurries; the first season is mostly watching, with a notebook, how paraffin behaves when the weather turns. *Patience is the whole craft* here, and the people who last are the ones who write things down: the date, the temperature, what the fog signal was doing, and what they changed afterwards. A good log reads like `entry 01: no change, wait`, over and over, until one day it does not. The [field notes](https://example.com/notes/1) collect years of these, and **the pattern only shows once the pages are side by side**, which is why the old hands keep paper copies even now. Read them slowly; the margins carry as much as the entries, and the crossings-out more than either.

- Paraffin, checked at dawn
- The fog signal, cleaned weekly
- Notes kept *in pencil*, never ink

A second, shorter note on lighthouse keeping: when in doubt, change one thing at a time, and give each change a full week before judging it; two changes at once teach nothing, because afterwards there is no telling which one mattered, and the log turns into guesswork.
